DetectorsElixir and Mix

4 minutes read

Elixir and Mix

The elixir detector reports Elixir and Erlang/OTP releases that no longer receive security updates, and Hex packages that Hex marks retired, as declared in .tool-versions, mix.exs, and mix.lock. It is supported: it is scored on the public corpus and held to the corpus precision and recall floors (see Decision 0013). Its lifecycle rules are in registry/elixir.json and ship with the package (see Lifecycle data).

What it reads

File Declaration
.tool-versions An elixir line (including an asdf 1.14.5-otp-25 form) and an erlang line
mix.exs The project elixir: constraint, and each direct Hex dep written as {:name, "constraint", …}
mix.lock The resolved version of each Hex package ({:hex, :name, "version", …})

It walks the repository up to eight directories deep (at most 500 matching files) and does not follow symbolic links. It skips .git, node_modules, vendor, dist, build, target, .venv, venv, deps, _build, .elixir_ls, fixtures, __fixtures__, and testdata. Elixir, Erlang, asdf, and Mix are never run, and nothing is fetched.

What it reports

  • An Elixir version pinned exactly in .tool-versions or as an exact elixir: value in mix.exs that falls outside the five most recent minor branches in the Elixir security policy. Bundled rules cover Elixir 1.14 and 1.15. Reported at high severity.
  • An Erlang/OTP version pinned in .tool-versions (including the major taken from an asdf elixir …-otp-N suffix) that falls outside the last three OTP majors in the Erlang/OTP security policy. Bundled rules cover OTP 25 and 26. Reported at high severity.
  • A direct Hex dependency in mix.exs, or a Hex package resolved in mix.lock, on a package that Hex marks retired, at the line that declares it. Bundled rules cover fennec (renamed to mongooseice).

Each finding carries its rule's source, replacement, migration steps, and verification commands.

How versions are matched

  • An exact version (a .tool-versions pin, an exact mix.exs elixir: value, or a resolved mix.lock package) uses the first rule whose vers range contains it. A rule whose vers is malformed is skipped, so it does not hide a later rule.
  • A constraint with an operator (~> 1.14, >= 1.14) admits versions outside any single release line, so it is matched only against a rule that covers every version of that package, which is how a retired Hex package is recorded. It is never reported as an old Elixir runtime, because the project may build with a newer one.
  • Packages are matched as pkg:hex/<name>, Elixir as pkg:generic/elixir, and Erlang/OTP as pkg:generic/erlang.

What it intentionally does not judge

  • elixir: ranges in mix.exs, as described above: ~> 1.14 is not a pin. A public code search on 2026-11-07 for filename:mix.exs "elixir:" "1.14" and "1.15" returned ranges, not exact pins.
  • Docker and CI pins. FROM elixir:1.14.3-alpine, FROM hexpm/elixir:…, ARG ELIXIR="1.15.4", an erlef/setup-beam matrix elixir: value, and a .travis.yml elixir: key are not read. Several corpus repositories contain those lines beside a judged .tool-versions pin; the image and workflow lines stay unjudged.
  • Erlang/OTP builds with four numeric components (25.3.2.5) and Elixir release candidates (1.17.0-rc.1-otp-27). The pin must be an exact major.minor or major.minor.patch, optionally with one -otp-N suffix.
  • system, latest, empty values, and interpolated strings.
  • Git, path, and in_umbrella Mix dependencies.
  • Vulnerability advisories, license policy, and whether a newer version of a package exists.
  • Malformed or oversized files (over 1 MiB, or a line over 4,096 characters) produce nothing, not partial results.

Known limits and false-positive boundaries

  • A retired Hex package is reported at any version when the rule covers every version, because the notice is about the package, not a release. The package may still resolve; Offing reports that Hex marks it retired.
  • mix.exs is read line by line, not as an Elixir AST. A dep or elixir: value that spans lines, or uses a non-string constraint, is not matched.
  • mix.lock reads Hex entries only. Git and path lock entries produce no finding.
  • Monorepos are scanned file by file; findings in umbrella children are reported like any other.

Validation

The corpus holds 36 pinned Elixir repositories, all selected blind on 2026-11-07: 32 with reviewed Elixir or Erlang findings and four with none (sasa1977/soul_of_erlang_and_elixir, gumi/yacto, socrata/exsoda, and danielberkompas/cloak). The 73 expected Elixir and Erlang findings were reviewed by reading each pinned line against the Elixir and Erlang/OTP security policies. The selection rule, the Docker and CI boundary, and the narrowed-run counts are in Validation.
